Mutation models

Source: R/model.R
mutation.Rd

  • mutation(): for additive() and multilinear() architectures; hoc_mutation() is the house of cards version (persistence = 0). Each allele mutates with probability rate per generation; a mutation adds a draw from a multivariate normal with mean zero and covariance cov to the allele's effect vector.

  • contribution_mutation(): for contribution_matrix(). Each allele of a weight gene mutates with probability rate_weight, each allele of a contribution gene with rate_contribution; a mutation adds Normal(0, sd) to the allele's value.

  • binary_b_mutation(): for binary_b(). Each allele's effect y mutates with probability rate, adding Normal(0, sd); each entry of B mutates with probability rate_b. With b_mutation = "flip" (the default, and the current C code) a mutated entry always changes; with "random" it gets a random value, 0 or 1, so it changes half of the time, as in the C code used for the simulations of Melo & Marroig (2015).

Usage

mutation(rate, cov, persistence = 1)

hoc_mutation(rate, cov)

contribution_mutation(rate_weight, rate_contribution, sd, persistence = 1)

binary_b_mutation(
  rate,
  sd,
  rate_b,
  b_mutation = c("flip", "random"),
  persistence = 1
)

Arguments

rate

mutation probability per allele per generation.

cov

mutational covariance matrix (traits x traits), or a single number \(s\), meaning \(s^2 I\).

persistence

how much of the old effect a mutation keeps: the new effect is \(\rho e + \delta\), with \(\rho\) = persistence, \(e\) the old effect and \(\delta\) a fresh draw. 1 (the default) is a random walk, where mutational effects accumulate; 0 is the house of cards model (Kingman 1978; Turelli 1984), where a mutation replaces the effect with a fresh draw unrelated to it; values in between give a regression towards the reference genotype (Zeng & Cockerham 1993). For binary_b() it applies to y.

rate_weight, rate_contribution

mutation probability per allele per generation of weight genes and of contribution genes.

sd

standard deviation of mutations in y.

rate_b

mutation probability per entry of B per generation.

b_mutation

"random" or "flip", see above.

Value

An evomod_mutation object.

Examples

mutation(rate = 0.005, cov = 0.05)
#> $type
#> [1] "gaussian"
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 0.005
#> 
#> $cov
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $persistence
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "evomod_mutation"
hoc_mutation(rate = 0.005, cov = 0.5)   # house of cards
#> $type
#> [1] "gaussian"
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 0.005
#> 
#> $cov
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $persistence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "evomod_mutation"
binary_b_mutation(rate = 0.0005, sd = 0.2, rate_b = 0.0001)
#> $type
#> [1] "binary_b"
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 5e-04
#> 
#> $sd
#> [1] 0.2
#> 
#> $rate_b
#> [1] 1e-04
#> 
#> $b_mutation
#> [1] "flip"
#> 
#> $random_state
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $persistence
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "evomod_mutation"
mutation(rate = 0.005, cov = matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1), 2) * 0.01)
#> $type
#> [1] "gaussian"
#> 
#> $rate
#> [1] 0.005
#> 
#> $cov
#>       [,1]  [,2]
#> [1,] 0.010 0.005
#> [2,] 0.005 0.010
#> 
#> $persistence
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "evomod_mutation"
